findings.description: The integrity check now counts index entries rather than files present on disk. Deleting a tracked .claude file without staging the deletion leaves git ls-files unchanged, so EXPECTED_COUNT still equals ACTUAL_COUNT.
findings.failure_mode: A checkout missing tracked System Zone scripts or configuration passes this integrity check without the mismatch warning previously emitted for missing files.
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate tracked paths in MANIFEST_TREE, but count only paths that actually exist in that working tree, or explicitly report missing tracked paths before comparing counts.

findings.description: check_integrity now ends with an unconditional `return 0`. Before this change the function's status was that of `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...`, so a Tampered/Missing path made the function return 1 (and under `set -e` aborted the script non-zero). After the change the exit code of check-loa.sh depends entirely on `fail` recording state in a global that main() later inspects; the diff does not show `fail`, so this cannot be confirmed from the hunk.
findings.failure_mode: If `fail` only prints, a tampered or missing System Zone file is reported on stdout but check-loa.sh exits 0, and any caller (CI, preflight, mount scripts) that gates on the exit code treats a drifted tree as healthy.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `fail` increments a counter/flag that main() turns into a non-zero exit. If it does not, replace `return 0` with `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]]` (or `return $([[ $drift == true ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)`) and add a bats case asserting non-zero exit on a tampered file.

findings.description: The not-mounted branch classifies any manifest path that is absent from `.claude/` as informational whenever `.loa/.claude` is a directory and `.loa/<path>` exists. It cannot distinguish a path the mount never linked (by design) from a link that was later removed. The only tamper signal that survives in a submodule mount is a hash mismatch on a file that is still present.
findings.failure_mode: Deleting a linked System Zone script or hook in a submodule mount (accidentally or deliberately) downgrades from `Missing` (fail) to a single `not-mounted: N path(s)` summary line that never changes the exit code, so the integrity check passes.
findings.suggested_fix: If the mount writes a list of what it linked (e.g. a mount-scope/link manifest), compare against that: absent AND listed as linked -> Missing; absent AND not listed -> not-mounted. Failing that, at least print the first few not-mounted paths so a reviewer can spot an unexpected one.

findings.description: The row builder emits `name`, `model_requested` and `models_used` straight from pipeline.json phases without defaults, while `--validate` in the same script requires `name` string, `model_requested` string and `models_used` object (and `effort_requested` string|null). Every other numeric field is defaulted (`// 0`), but these three are not. A phase record from a run that died before the executor returned a result (agent_error, interrupted, docker failure) plausibly has `models_used: null`.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-row.sh writes a row that its own `--validate` rejects (`phases[i]: field models_used has type null, want object`), so a batch runs.jsonl fails validation on the first crashed phase and downstream spend/took-effect consumers refuse the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the emitted fields to the validator's shape: `models_used: (.models_used // {})`, `model_requested: (.model_requested // "")`, `name: (.name // .label // "")`. Add a bats fixture run with a phase that has no result JSON and assert the row validates.

findings.description: `ms(ts)` strips only a `.NNN Z` fractional suffix and then calls `fromdateiso8601`, which accepts exactly `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`. A `started`/`finished` value with a numeric offset (`+00:00`, as produced by `date -Is`/`date --iso-8601=seconds`) or with fractional seconds and no trailing Z raises a jq error. Because the whole row is one `jq -n` call under `set -euo pipefail`, that error aborts the script with jq's exit status 5 and no diagnostic, outside the documented 0/1/2 exit codes.
findings.failure_mode: A timestamp format drift in pipeline-run.sh (or a run whose meta was written on a host with a different `date` default) makes ablation-row.sh exit 5 silently for every run, and the batch runner, which keys off exit 2 for usage errors, misclassifies it.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise timestamps before parsing (`sub("(\\.[0-9]+)?(Z|[+-]00:?00)$"; "Z")`) or compute wall clock in bash with `date -d`. Wrap the ROW build in `|| usage "row build failed: ..."` so a jq failure maps to exit 2 with a message.

findings.description: `norm_model` strips the Bedrock region/vendor prefix and a trailing `-vN[:M]`, but not the dated release segment Bedrock ids carry (e.g. `anthropic.claude-fable-5-1-20260101-v1:0` vs requested `claude-fable-5-1`), nor OpenAI dated ids (`gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` vs `gpt-5.5`) that the pricing ladder in test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py explicitly treats as the same model. Any such pair is reported as a model mismatch.
findings.failure_mode: Every Bedrock or dated-id run is marked `degraded: true` with a spurious `model X used, Y requested` reason, which poisons the degraded signal the ablation analysis (took-effect, spend) relies on to exclude bad runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend `norm_model` to also strip `-[0-9]{8}` and `-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}` suffixes, or reuse the pricing ladder's dated/alias normalisation so model identity is decided in one place.

findings.description: `tool_version` captures `2>&1` and keeps the first line. Several of the listed tools write advisory text to stderr before or instead of the version (node deprecation/NODE_OPTIONS warnings, claude/codex update-available notices, docker daemon-unreachable errors). Whichever line appears first becomes the recorded version, and `docker=` in particular flips between a version and an error string depending on whether the daemon is up.
findings.failure_mode: The same host produces different `fp:` digests across runs in one batch, so `host_fingerprint`/`image_digest` stop identifying a toolchain and runs that should be comparable get split, or runs on different toolchains collide when both record `unknown`.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture stdout only (`2>/dev/null`) and fall back to stderr only when stdout is empty; for docker use `docker --version` (client-only, already the case) but strip to the `Docker version X` token with a regex rather than the whole first line. Record the raw lines in `--json` for debugging.

findings.description: The source-tree component of the fingerprint is `git rev-parse HEAD` alone. Uncommitted edits in the pinned Loa tree (the very thing freeze.sh/toggles mutate) do not change the fingerprint.
findings.failure_mode: Two batches run against the same HEAD but different working-tree contents of the source tree record identical `fingerprint`/`image_digest`, so the reproducibility field in MANIFEST.json and runs.jsonl silently vouches for runs that were not equivalent.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold in `git -C "$SOURCE_TREE" status --porcelain | sha256` (or `git diff HEAD | sha256`) as a `source_tree_dirty=<hash|clean>` line, or refuse (`exit 2`) when the tree is dirty unless `--allow-dirty` is passed.

findings.cross_file_justification: The codex-headless hop (diff-touched, cli_model -> gpt-6.1-sol) now prices every estimated MODELINV/cost-ledger row through this placeholder entry; the test file in the diff (test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py) locks that resolution in.
findings.description: gpt-6.1-sol pricing is an acknowledged copy of gpt-5.5 list prices. Because the codex hop's estimates and MODELINV rows resolve through it, every cost figure the ablation harness aggregates for OpenAI CLI phases (ledger_cost_usd, voice_cost_usd, and the spend caps built on them) is computed from a rate card that is known to be unconfirmed. Nothing in the row marks these as placeholder-priced beyond the generic `cost_estimated` flag.
findings.failure_mode: If the real gpt-6.1 rate differs materially, spend caps enforce against the wrong number for the whole Sprint 258/259 batch and the recorded cost_usd in runs.jsonl is wrong in a way that cannot be corrected after the fact without re-deriving from token counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `pricing.placeholder: true` (or `pricing_source: placeholder`) marker the ledger can carry into rows, so spend.sh can treat placeholder-priced spend conservatively and the bead that confirms the rate card has a mechanical trigger to clear. At minimum, keep raw token counts on the ledger rows so cost can be recomputed once confirmed.

findings.description: `git ls-files -- .claude` counts index entries, not working-tree files: paths deleted from the worktree without `git rm` are still counted, and symlink entries count as one each. In a mount where `.claude` itself is a tracked symlink to the submodule tree, `.claude/checksums.json` is not itself a link (`-L` is false through a symlinked directory), so MANIFEST_TREE stays at PROJECT_ROOT and the count is 1, which is non-zero and therefore does not trigger the `find` fallback.
findings.failure_mode: The file-count integrity warning fires on every preflight for whole-directory symlink mounts, and is suppressed (count still matches) when a tracked `.claude/` file has been removed from disk, which is the case the check exists to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `.claude` itself with `readlink -f` before deciding MANIFEST_TREE, and filter `git ls-files` output through `[[ -e ]]` (or use `git ls-files --deleted` to subtract) so the count reflects files actually present.
